is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae s.l. (An. arabiensis, An. coluzzii, An. gambiae s.s.) and An. rufipes larvae collected in Kenya (page 2, 9).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study reports genotyping for Vgsc L1014F (kdr-west) (page 7, 17).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 2 (page 17) provides genotype counts (RR, RS, SS) for L1014F in An. arabiensis and An. coluzzii across different sites.

african_field_population.evidence: The study collected mosquito larvae from field sites in Dadaab, Kakuma, and Kalobeyei refugee camps in Kenya (page 2, 5).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study reporting original larval survey and genotyping data (page 5, 8, 17).

sub_country_location.evidence: The study specifies locations as Dadaab, Kakuma, and Kalobeyei refugee camps in Kenya (page 2, 8).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study states collections were conducted between May and July 2023 (page 2, 5).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study reports new larval collections from 2023.

supplement.evidence: All necessary genotype data is provided in Table 2.

assessment.summary: This study conducted larval surveys in three Kenyan refugee camps (Dadaab, Kakuma, and Kalobeyei) in 2023. It identified Anopheles arabiensis, An. coluzzii, An. gambiae s.s., and An. rufipes. Genotyping for the Vgsc L1014F (kdr-west) mutation revealed high frequencies in An. coluzzii in Turkana County (Kakuma/Kalobeyei) and lower frequencies in An. arabiensis, while no kdr mutations were found in Dadaab.
